svg.text: Edge-launch wing socket — hub_board_v9, J_W1…J_W4
COMMITTED GEOMETRY — ADR-048: a routed slot 0.9 × 6.0 mm in the hub edge (0.9 mm wide, 6.0 mm deep), the 0.6 mm tab seated 6.0 mm into it, the four lands on the slot's faces, the fillet
loaded in SHEAR. The ±0.10 mm tolerance is PROPOSED (see Q3) and the CONSTRUCTION of the slot-face lands is UNVERIFIED (see Q6).

ADR-046 §4.2.2: "Option A is the committed geometry". The BOARD AS BUILT implements Option B — no slot, J_W* lands on F.Cu only (ADR-046 §4.2.1, measured). THE BOARD CHANGE IS PENDING: this sheet depicts the
committed geometry and must not be read as the built state.

through the land row: the four lands at 1.8 mm pitch and the two shear-loaded fillets · SCHEMATIC laterally

View A — what the numbers on this view are
hub material — the board either side of, and beyond, the slot. Its LATERAL extent is SCHEMATIC: no record we hold
fixes it, and the hub's own thickness is TODO(unverified) (ADR-048 §5). See the sheet-scope row
the ROUTED FACE of the slot — a CUT face. The pad-face ENIG (F.Cu / B.Cu at the hub's outer faces) does not
establish a finish on copper newly exposed by routing. Asked as Q1; NOT answered on this sheet
the lands on the slot's faces — 4 per face, 4.0 mm along the insertion axis, 1.2 mm across at 1.8 mm pitch
(ADR-048 §2.2). Copper is drawn a little thicker than scale (it is 35 µm, 1 oz, on a 0.6 mm board) so the section
reads. NO construction that produces broad copper on an internal routed face is established by any record we hold
— the lands are drawn UNVERIFIED; asked as Q6
the solder fillets — the gap between a slot face and the tab's copper on that face. ADR-046 §4.1's 0.30 mm total
(slot 0.9 − tab 0.6) is NOMINAL, computed on BARE substrate; the tab's copper on each face narrows the FINISHED
gap, and the finished gap is what is DRAWN here. Loaded in SHEAR on both faces, which is why Option A's capacity
is the joint's anchor (ADR-046 §4.2.2)
the wing tab — 0.6 mm FR4 SUBSTRATE (ADR-046 §4.1), 8.0 mm long, seated 6.0 mm into the slot so 2.0 mm stays
outside. Its tip is relieved to match the slot's routed end, so it seats to the full 6.0 mm — but that relief and the
slot's end radius are NOT fixed by any record we hold, and the semicircle drawn here is an ILLUSTRATION, not a
specification: the full 6.0 mm seating is a REQUIREMENT, not a verified fit. Asked as Q7. The tab carries COPPER on
each face (35 µm, 1 oz), drawn on the substrate's OUTER faces here; the tab's FINISH is not fixed by a record we
hold (Q1). The FINISHED tab is thicker than 0.6 mm — see the tab-stack-up row
the slot's mouth reaches the outline ON THE SLOT'S CENTRE LINE (ADR-048 §2.5: "the land IS the interface"). The
land copper runs 1.0 … 5.0 mm inboard of that edge (ADR-048 D-1). The slot's inner end is ROUNDED — a cutter
radius, not a square end; see Q7
View B — what the numbers on this view are
the four lands, seen END-ON: 1.2 mm across at 1.8 mm pitch, 0.6 mm clear between lands. Their 4.0
mm extent runs NORMAL to this view — dimensioned in View A. Each is a SEPARATE conductor: the
tab-face copper is broken at every 0.6 mm gap, so W1_SOLAR_P, GND, W1_RF and W1_SOLAR_N are
NOT connected to one another on either face
one fillet per land per face, wetting that land's 4.0 mm. The 4.0 mm runs along the insertion axis, i.e.
NORMAL to this view. The lane DRAWN is the FINISHED gap: slot 0.9 − (0.6 mm substrate + a copper
layer on each face). ADR-046 §4.1's 0.15 mm per face is NOMINAL on bare substrate and is wider — see
the tab-stack-up row
the hub material either side of the slot. Its extent is SCHEMATIC — no record we hold fixes how far the
slot runs along the hub edge, only its 0.9 mm width and 6.0 mm depth
the 9.0 mm tab: 4 × 1.2 mm lands + 3 × 0.6 mm gaps + 2 × 1.2 mm of tab beyond the outer lands
(ADR-048 §2.2). That 1.2 mm is the TAB's own margin, NOT a tab-to-slot-wall clearance — no record
fixes that clearance, so none is drawn or claimed here
Requirements and questions for the fabricator
Sheet scope
This sheet depicts the COMMITTED hub-side interface geometry for fabrication review. It is TWO SECTIONS: nothing outside them is drawn — no solder-mask geometry, no
plan view, no keep-out outline. It does NOT fix the hub's outline, thickness or layer count, the component keep-out at the slot, the slot's extent along the hub edge, or any
price — none of those is fixed by a record we hold, and none is asserted here.
Committed geometry
Routed slot 0.9 x 6.0 mm in the hub edge, 0.6 mm tab seated 6.0 mm into it, the four lands on the slot's faces, the fillet loaded in SHEAR on BOTH faces. This is ADR-048
§2.2 / ADR-046 §4.2.2 — the COMMITTED geometry for this interface.
Slot tolerance
±0.10 mm is PROPOSED, not a cited figure (ADR-046 §4.3 records it as an assumption). ADR-048 §2.2 states it alongside "0.9 mm wide × 6.0 mm deep"; whether it applies
to the depth as well as the width is not fixed by any record we hold. QUESTION Q3.
State of the board
The board as built implements Option B: NO slot, J_W1…J_W4 lands on F.Cu only, fillet in peel (ADR-046 §4.2.1, measured with
tracker/hardware/introspect_edge_interface.py). The change to the slot is PENDING. This sheet is not a statement that the board is already slotted.
Surface finish — pad faces
ENIG preferred on F.Cu / B.Cu: flat and solderable after assembly. HASL is acceptable. This is the finish on the LAND, at the hub's outer faces.
Surface finish — routed faces
NOT established by the pad-face finish. Copper newly exposed by routing the slot is on a CUT face, which the pad's mask opening and finish do not cover. We are asking, not
asserting — QUESTION Q1.
Solder mask
The four lands are drawn as bare copper, so NO solder-mask geometry is drawn on this sheet at all: whether a mask opening is required on the routed faces is part of the
same open question as their finish (Q1), and the sheet does not assert a mask either way. The component keep-out is a PLACEMENT constraint, not interface geometry, and
is not drawn — see the sheet-scope row.
Copper at the interface
The slot's MOUTH reaches the outline ON THE SLOT'S CENTRE LINE — ADR-048 §2.5: "the land IS the interface". The land copper runs 1.0 … 5.0 mm inboard of that edge
(ADR-048 D-1, as in the committed footprint), so on this geometry the copper is NOT flush with the routed edge. On the Option-B board as built it is flush at the edge — that
is the as-built state, not this one.
NOT wanted
No castellation, no edge plating, no plated slot barrel — a plated slot would short the lands around the tab. Plain exposed copper on a plain routed cut.
Land construction — UNVERIFIED
The four lands on the slot's faces are drawn as copper because ADR-048 §2.2 places them there, but HOW they are produced, and which copper layer they are part of, is
NOT established by any record we hold. No plating is wanted. UNVERIFIED — do not treat the drawn lands as a fabricable construction. QUESTION Q6.
Tab stack-up
The 0.6 mm is the tab's FR4 SUBSTRATE thickness (ADR-046 §4.1) and it is what the View B dimension measures — the tab's copper is drawn on the substrate's OUTER
faces, outside that span. The tab carries a copper layer on each face, drawn on both sections at 35 µm (1 oz) per the board stack-up, of which the four 4.0 × 1.2 mm lands
are the solderable patches. The FINISHED tab is thicker by that copper and its finish, so the finished solder gap is narrower than the 0.30 mm nominal. The tab's FINISH is
not fixed by a record we hold — the same class of question as the routed face, so it is included in QUESTION Q1.
Mating fit — UNVERIFIED
The finished tab thickness, the slot's width and depth tolerances, the finished solder clearances, the slot-end radius and the tab-tip relief are NOT fixed by any record we
hold — they are design decisions. They are shown UNVERIFIED — under query (Q7); no value for any of them is invented here.
Routed edge positional tolerance
Routed edge and slot relative to copper — please advise your capability. QUESTION Q2.
Minimum routable slot
A repo note records a minimum non-plated slot of ~1.0 mm, i.e. above our 0.9 mm (placement freeze, §4). We do not know whether that is current or correct for this build —
please confirm, since a 0.9 mm slot is the committed geometry. QUESTION Q4.
Routed cut-out cost
The slot adds a routing line item. We hold no price and ask for yours; nothing here is a claim about your pricing. QUESTION Q5.
Panel tabs
Keep tabs clear of these edges. They are mating surfaces and a tab there would ruin the contact.
Burrs / peeling
Please advise mitigation if the cut produces them at the interface, and whether a finish on the cut face changes that.
Alignment caveat (design)
The slot BOUNDS the attach angle; it does NOT key it. ADR-046 §4.2.2's figure is BARE-SUBSTRATE: 0.30 mm of play over a 6.0 mm insertion is 2.86°, i.e. 8.79 mm of
wing-tip movement at 176 mm. With the tab's copper on each face the finished play is narrower — 0.30 − 2 × 0.035 ≈ 0.23 mm, ≈ 2.20° / 6.74 mm — and finish and
tolerances narrow it further. The 90° angle is a FIXTURING requirement, and this sheet does not claim otherwise.
Q1 routed-face finish
Routing the slot exposes copper on a cut face. Does your process put any finish on that face? If the pad faces are ENIG, is the copper at the routed face (a) covered by the
same finish, (b) bare copper, or (c) something else? Please say which, and how we must specify it to get what you describe. The wing TAB carries copper on its faces too and
its finish is likewise not fixed by a record we hold — please answer for the tab's faces as well.
Q2 tolerance
What positional tolerance can you hold between the routed edge/slot and the copper lands?
Q3 slot tolerance
What width tolerance can you hold on a 0.9 mm routed slot? Does the same tolerance apply to its 6.0 mm depth?
Q4 minimum slot
What is your minimum routable non-plated slot width? If 0.9 mm is below it, what is the smallest you will rout, and does that change if the slot is plated?
Q5 cost
What is the additional cost of an internal routed cut-out on this order, as a line item?
Q6 copper on the slot faces
Our lands sit on the two OPPOSED INTERNAL ROUTED-SLOT FACES (4.0 × 1.2 mm per face). We are NOT identifying them as outer-layer F.Cu / B.Cu — those are the hub's
EXTERNAL copper layers, a different surface. HOW that copper is produced and WHICH layer it connects to is UNRESOLVED by any record we hold, so we assert no
construction. We do NOT want a plated slot barrel. Please tell us what to specify, and say if what we have drawn is not producible.
Q7 slot end radius
A routed slot's inner end carries the cutter's radius. What radius will our 0.9 mm slot end have, and what relief or clearance must the mating tab's tip have to seat against
it? We have drawn a semicircular end as an illustration, not as a specification.

Committed geometry: docs/adr/048-v9-hub-wing-interfaces.md §2.2 (slot 0.9 × 6.0 mm, keep-out slot outline + 1.0 mm) and docs/adr/046-wing-board-interface.md §4.1/§4.2.2. Board state measured by tracker/hardware/introspect_edge_interface.py.
